LESSON: INTENSIVE READING: SHORT STORY (CLASS READER)

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.1: Intensive Reading: Short story (Class Reader)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Intensive Reading: Short story (Class Reader), part of Strand 4 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8 ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: How does one identify qualities of characters in a short story?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify the characters in a given short story

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Intensive Reading: Short story (Class Reader) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. explain the relationship between the characters in the short story

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Intensive Reading: Short story (Class Reader) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate the role of the characters in the short story in depicting real-life experiences. • Read the short story and pick out the characters, Learners who may not turn pages to use page turners or be supported by peers. • Discuss the things done by the characters in the short story, Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech as they are lip read by the teacher or peers. Dramatise different characters in a short story in order to bring out their traits, Create a conducive environment and adequate space for learners with mobility difficulties and ensure safety for all learners as they perform the activity. Assign roles according to each learners abilities. • Distinguish between the main characters and the minor characters, How does one identify qualities of characters in a short story? 65 • Work with peers to use relationship trees diagrams, character map or any other diagrammatic tool to show how the characters relate to each other, • Display the tree diagram via power point or manila paper in class.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Intensive Reading: Short story (Class Reader) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking is enhanced as the learner uses logical reasoning while discussing the actions of the characters.

• Creativity and imagination is enhanced as the learner shows the relationships between characters in the story.

Values:
Responsibility is promoted as the learner engages and helps peers as they work in groups.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Social cohesion is promoted as learners observe the rules of engagement while dramatising different characters in a short story.

Link to other subjects:

The learner is able to relate the concept of characterisation to character analysis in Religious studies.
